facts.text: Street medicine vendors are dangerously filling Haiti’s healthcare gaps
Image by Global Voices, created using Canva elements.
Haiti is a country with very few health facilities and a dearth of healthcare workers to meet people’s needs.
Public hospitals lack basic medical equipment, demand far exceeds staff capacity, and administrative problems are rife.

Other health centres, usually run by non-profit organisations, help some of the most vulnerable people, while private hospitals are few and far between, given that most Haitians cannot afford to pay for treatment there.
Even the wealthy are often forced to go abroad for treatment when faced with critical health issues.

This already dire situation became worse when gangs from the Viv Ansanm criminal coalition began targeting both public and private health facilities, looting many of them, stealing equipment, and even setting fire to some of the properties.
Health centres located in gang-controlled areas are often forced to close temporarily because of fights that break out between rival gangs.

stories.summary: The Rt Hon Pat McFadden MP, Secretary of State for Work and Pensions, responded to the publication of the independent Milburn review into young people and work. This morning, Alan Milburn published a landmark report, setting out a radical blueprint for a new settlement with young people. facts.text: Work and Pensions Secretary statement on the Milburn review into young people and work
The Rt Hon Pat McFadden MP, Secretary of State for Work and Pensions, responded to the publication of the independent Milburn review into young people and work.
With your permission, Mr Speaker, I would like to make a statement on the Milburn review into young people and work.
This morning, Alan Milburn published a landmark report, setting out a radical blueprint for a new settlement with young people.
I want to thank Mr Milburn and his team for their outstanding work.
Sometimes a review deals with an issue so fundamental that it alters what we see as the contract between Government and society.
Because one million young people not in education, employment or training creates a human cost that no country should ask its young people to bear.
It robs them of the thing that is most important to their lives – the prospect of a good future.

on_this_day.title: The Suez Canal opens
on_this_day.summary: The Suez Canal officially opened on 17 November 1869. Located in Egypt, it connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea. Ships using the canal can travel between these seas without sailing around southern Africa. The opening was a significant moment in the history of maritime transport. The canal also has a complex political history, showing how a piece of infrastructure can matter to both travel and international affairs.
